testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, the spring brakes should come on automatically when:
questions.explanation: Spring brakes should come on when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. To test this, chock the wheels and release air by pressing the brake pedal on and off. When pressure drops to an unsafe level, the parking brake valve should pop out and spring brakes should engage.

questions.question: Foundation brakes are used at:
questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are located at each wheel. The most common type is the S-cam drum brake.

questions.question: How should you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Turn the parking brake on and off.
Press and release the brake pedal rapidly.
Disconnect and reconnect all glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and release the brake pedal rapidly.
questions.explanation: Your low pressure warning light must work properly. After the system charges, press and release the brake pedal rapidly. This releases air from the system. The warning signal should come on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: Test the low pressure warning signal:
questions.explanation: Your low pressure warning light must work properly. After the system charges, press and release the brake pedal rapidly. This releases air from the system. The warning signal should come on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.

questions.question: When inspecting your brakes, a slack adjuster should move ____ from where it connects to the push rod.
questions.explanation: After chocking the wheels and disengaging the parking brake, check each slack adjuster. Pull the slack adjusters to make sure they move no more than about one inch. If they move more than one inch, they need adjustment.

questions.question: The parking brake should be:
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake in a vehicle with air brakes whenever you park.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheel lockup during hard braking. This provides better control. However, ABS does not always shorten stopping distance.

questions.question: To inspect slack adjusters on S-cam brakes, you need to:

options.text: Park on a hill and test the brakes.
Put on gloves and push the slack adjusters in.
Remove the drum and look inside.
Chock the wheels and disengage the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Chock the wheels and disengage the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Park on level ground, set wheel chocks, and disengage the parking brake. Then pull the slack adjusters to check they do not move more than about one inch. If they move more than one inch, they need adjustment.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning light comes on while driving:

options.text: Braking works only if there is still enough air in the tanks.
You can apply the brakes 14 times before all air runs out.
Continue driving and check the brakes later.
Stay at least 100 feet away from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Braking works only if there is still enough air in the tanks.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning light comes on while driving, stop and safely park as soon as possible. There may be a leak. You can still brake, but only as long as enough air remains in the tanks.

questions.question: Water and compressor oil are usually found in compressed air within an air brake system. These should:

options.text: Be kept in the system for proper brake function.

questions.explanation: Compressed air usually contains water and compressor oil. If left in the system, they can damage the brakes. Open the manual air tank drains daily to remove this build-up.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). Other vehicles with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1998 must also have ABS.

questions.question: A tank endorsement is needed to:
questions.explanation: You need a tank endorsement to drive a tank vehicle that carries liquids or gases.

questions.question: When spring brakes are activated, you should never:

options.text: Release air from the air storage tanks.

questions.explanation: Do not press the brake pedal when spring brakes are active. The brakes can be damaged if both springs and air pressure are applied at the same time.

questions.question: Brake fade happens because of:
questions.explanation: When brakes are used too much, they overheat and become less effective. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: In a newer vehicle, you use the parking brake by:
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake uses a diamond-shaped yellow knob. Pull the knob out to apply the brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: The air compressor governor controls:

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks.
The temperature of air in the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor decides when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: Controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
Controls how quickly air leaves the storage tanks.
Controls the temperature of air entering the storage tanks.
Controls the temperature of air leaving the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor decides when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal unnecessarily can:

options.text: Release air faster than the compressor can replace it.
Add more air to the braking system.
Make the brake pedal more sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air faster than the compressor can replace it.
questions.explanation: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal unnecessarily can release air from the system faster than the compressor can refill it.

questions.question: The air entering storage tanks may contain:
questions.explanation: Air entering storage tanks usually contains water and compressor oil. These materials can damage the braking system, so tanks have drains to remove them.

questions.question: The most common foundation brake is:
questions.explanation: The S-cam drum brake is the most common type of foundation brake.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use:
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. This means two separate air brake systems controlled by one set of controls.

questions.question: Brakes can get out of adjustment if:

options.text: Brakes on one side are used more than brakes on the other side.

questions.explanation: Brakes are likely to get out of adjustment when they are hot. Use proper braking techniques to keep your brakes from overheating.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
Clean the air in the passenger area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains that remove water and compressor oil. Water and oil in the system can damage the brakes. Drains should be used daily.

questions.question: The air storage tanks:

options.text: Hold air for only one brake use.
Hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor fails.
Hold air only during an emergency.
Hold enough air for more than 1,000 brake uses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor fails.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: A one-way check valve:

options.text: Drains water and compressor oil from the air tanks.
Stops air from escaping if the air compressor leaks.
Turns on the emergency brakes when there is a leak.
Keeps the spring brakes in place until they are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from escaping if the air compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve must be placed between the air compressor and the main reservoir. This valve stops air from escaping the system if the air compressor leaks.
